Right, so, at the lab we have these air quality sensors, about thirty of them around the city, and they upload CSV files to an FTP box, well SFTP, every hour, and the files are honestly a mess, different firmware versions produce slightly different columns, some send duplicate rows when they reconnect, timestamps are in local time for some and UTC for others, it's a nightmare. What I need is a pipeline that picks up the new files every hour, normalizes all of that into one clean table, flags readings that are physically impossible, like negative particulate counts or jumps that have to be sensor faults, and loads the clean data into a Postgres database the analysis team already uses, they have Grafana on top of it. The thing I care about most is that I can re-run any day from scratch, like if we discover a bug in the normalization we re-process the last month and get exactly the same table, no duplicates, no drift. Um, and when a sensor goes quiet for more than three hours someone should get an email. It runs on one Linux VM we already have, the data is maybe, I don't know, a few hundred megabytes a month, nothing big. I'm the only data engineer, the team is three researchers who write SQL but not much else. No deadline pressure but I want it boring and reliable, I'm tired of the current pile of cron scripts.
